title: AI-assisted compressed sensing improved rectal MRI image-quality ratings in a small prospective study
summary: In 29 patients, AI-assisted compressed-sensing MRI received higher visibility, sharpness, and overall image-quality ratings than conventional acceleration methods at the same scan time. T-staging accuracy differences were not statistically significant; the single-center study does not establish improved clinical outcomes.
ai_technology: Deep-learning-assisted compressed-sensing reconstruction was used to produce rectal MRI images.
organization: Department of Radiology, The First Affiliated Hospital of Shandong First Medical University and Shandong Provincial Qianfoshan Hospital, Jinan, China

evidence.tested: Two radiologists compared three MRI sequences in 29 prospectively enrolled patients; image-quality measures favored AI-assisted reconstruction, while T-stage accuracy differences were not significant.
evidence.unknown: The small single-center study does not establish clinical benefit or generalizability.
evidence.ai_role: Deep-learning-assisted compressed-sensing reconstruction produced the evaluated rectal MRI sequences.

source_review.scope: Primary full-text review as recorded in case evidence; record-level claim and attribution review.
